# Cloud Provider Accounts: References

Always prefer current vendor documentation. Defaults, CLI flags, and console locations change often.
Re-verify links and contents when updating this skill.

Last verified: 2026-10-31

## Vendor (authoritative): AWS

- IAM security best practices: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html
- Root user best practices: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/root-user-best-practices.html
- MFA enforcement for root users across all account types (2025):
  https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/06/aws-iam-mfa-root-users-across-all-account-types
- Centralized root access management (Organizations):
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_root-user.html#id_root-user-access-management
- Credential reports: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_getting-report.html
- SecurityAudit and ViewOnlyAccess managed policies (job function policies):
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_job-functions.html
- S3 Block Public Access: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html
- Block public access for EBS snapshots: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html
- Block public access for AMIs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/block-public-access-to-amis.html
- AWS Budgets: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-managing-costs.html
- Cost Anomaly Detection: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html

  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantineV3.html
- AWS vulnerability reporting and abuse: https://aws.amazon.com/security/vulnerability-reporting/

## Third-party (not authoritative)

- Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, "Detecting exposed AWS IAM credentials" (timing of automatic quarantine):
  https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/detecting-exposed-aws-iam-credentials/
- Prowler and ScoutSuite (open-source multi-cloud scanners): useful checks; review the version and the
  permissions they need before running, and validate their findings.
- gitleaks and TruffleHog (open-source secret scanners): run only on the user's own repositories, with
  approval, and redact values in output.
